comment:urn:li:comment:(activity:7432772.text: That's the thing about culture — it's hard to understand how it works until you find yourself inside.

Every international market entry role I've taken started exactly this way — no playbook, no defined scope. The ambiguity isn't a bug, it's the job. The people who thrive in undefined roles are usually the ones who end up defining the function for everyone after them.

comment:urn:li:comment:(activity:7476214.text: I voted with the 💡Insightful emoji, as this reflects how one-on-ones with my manager feel.

comment:urn:li:comment:(activity:7498693.text: Life has definitely gotten more convenient, but it's sometimes really hard to keep the balance between letting AI help me and giving it the tiniest tasks that I could just do myself in 5 minutes and then getting annoyed that it doesn't understand what I want from it 😁

Andrii Rozhylo, while experiencing AI's positives and negatives and noticing shifts in my behavior, has helped me identify where to evolve while not letting AI become my hidden persona 😆 and thus a burden. 

A mentor writes on AI topics and you may find value in following her -> https://www.linkedin.com/in/carinknoop?utm_source=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=member_ios

Hello! I would like to ask if by any chance your business need a QA engineer who is easy to work with, who is having a good energy and who is ready to learn everything that the project requires (just as usual! ;) ). If the answer is "yes", would you please consider myself? Thank you! Cheers!

AI has definitely increased what I can produce, but the real productivity gain only happens when it reduces the number of decisions and reviews I have to carry - not when it simply gives me more output to process.
